species.label: E. coli
species.plain: A rod-shaped bacterium of the animal gut with 4,403 proteins in UniProt's reference proteome of strain K-12. The units of the law inventory are machines of animal cells; this is what the same families' signatures find in it.

method: The organism's proteins are the 4,403 reviewed entries of UniProt's reference proteome UP000000625 (release 2026_04), one protein each.
Licences were read before anything was copied; each is stated in sources.

A unit counts as found only where a protein carries the signature of a family that makes the machine itself (the subunit that forms the channel, or the pump's own chain). A protein that carries only the signature of a family that goes with the machine (a regulator, an accessory subunit) is no candidate: the unit's note names it, and it is listed under extra. This reading is the file's own.
Each unit's family was taken from its own human candidates, by the same InterPro signatures that the planarian, Syn3A and M. pneumoniae atlases ask. The build checks that the candidates carry them.
Each signature was looked for among the InterPro entries UniProt gives each of the 4,403 proteins. No unit's own family was found; 1 protein carries the signature of an accessory family alone.
A control for every signature: how many reviewed UniProtKB entries of all bacteria carry it; each unit's note gives what came back.

8 further signatures, of the channels a bacterium could have (potassium, chloride, magnesium, water and membrane-stretch channels), were looked for as well; the 15 proteins that carry them are listed under extra (the potassium channel domain (kch); the large-conductance mechanosensitive channel (MscL) (mscL); the mechanosensitive channel MscS (mscK, mscM, mscS, ybdG, ybiO and ynaI); chloride channels of the ClC family (clcA, clcB and yfeO); aquaporins and their relatives (major intrinsic proteins) (aqpZ and glpF); CorA-type magnesium channels (corA and zntB)), with the cell's P-type ATPases and the catalytic head of its ATP synthase.
No similarity search was run, and nothing is called an ortholog.

not_copied: No sequence is copied. Nothing is taken from the organism's own curated databases: EcoCyc's data files need a paid subscription, and STEPdb states no terms of use. Both are named in the note as places to read.

extra.name: Uncharacterized protein YfbK
extra.evidence_note: Its reviewed UniProtKB entry names it "Uncharacterized protein YfbK", with UniProt's level of evidence "predicted". The entry carries IPR051173 (Voltage-dependent calcium channel subunit alpha-2/delta).
extra.why: Carries the family signature of calcium channel alpha-2/delta subunits, which go with a channel and make none by themselves. No protein of this organism carries the signature of a family that makes such a channel, so it is a candidate for no unit (U24 to U30 asked for it).
